course.description: SAMPLE DATA. An introduction to the principles of artificial intelligence, covering intelligent agents, search, knowledge representation, reasoning under uncertainty, machine learning, and the ethical use of AI systems.

course_outcomes.text: Describe the foundational concepts, history, and applications of artificial intelligence.
Apply search and constraint satisfaction techniques to solve well-defined computational problems.
Construct logical and probabilistic representations of knowledge for reasoning under uncertainty.
Implement basic machine learning models and evaluate their performance using standard metrics.
Justify ethical and responsible design decisions in the development of AI systems.

weekly_schedule.topic: Introduction to AI and Intelligent Agents
weekly_schedule.description: Overview of the history, scope, and applications of AI, and the agent-environment model.

lesson_outcomes.text: Describe the history, goals, and major application areas of artificial intelligence.
Classify real-world agents by their environment properties and agent architecture.
Discuss the societal role of AI with respect for differing viewpoints.

weekly_schedule.description: Formulating problems as states, actions, goals, and path costs.

lesson_outcomes.text: Define the components of a well-formed search problem.
Formulate a given puzzle as a state-space search problem.
Demonstrate persistence in decomposing ambiguous problems into precise formal models.

weekly_schedule.description: Breadth-first, depth-first, uniform-cost, and iterative deepening search.

lesson_outcomes.text: Compare breadth-first and depth-first search in terms of completeness and complexity.
Implement breadth-first and depth-first search in Python for a maze problem.
Practice writing clean, documented code that peers can read and reproduce.

weekly_schedule.description: Greedy best-first search and A* search with admissible heuristics.

lesson_outcomes.text: Explain how admissible and consistent heuristics guarantee optimal A* search.
Implement A* search with a heuristic for a route-finding problem.
Justify heuristic design choices using evidence from experiments.

weekly_schedule.description: Hill climbing, simulated annealing, and genetic algorithms.

lesson_outcomes.text: Distinguish local search methods from systematic search methods.
Apply hill climbing and simulated annealing to an optimization problem.
Demonstrate willingness to revise solutions after analyzing failed runs.

weekly_schedule.description: Minimax and alpha-beta pruning for two-player games.

lesson_outcomes.text: Explain how minimax and alpha-beta pruning select moves in two-player games.
Implement a minimax player with alpha-beta pruning for tic-tac-toe.
Collaborate with teammates to test and improve game-playing agents.

weekly_schedule.description: Modeling problems with variables, domains, and constraints; backtracking and constraint propagation.

lesson_outcomes.text: Identify the variables, domains, and constraints in a given problem.
Solve a scheduling problem using backtracking with forward checking.
Demonstrate accuracy and attention to detail when specifying constraints.
Describe the syntax and semantics of propositional logic.
Translate English statements into propositional logic sentences.
Defend the need for unambiguous statements when specifying knowledge.

weekly_schedule.description: Review of Weeks 1 to 8 and midterm assessment.

lesson_outcomes.text: Recall the key search, game, and logic concepts covered in Weeks 1 to 8.
Solve search and constraint problems under timed conditions.
Demonstrate academic integrity during the examination.
Explain quantifiers, unification, and resolution in first-order logic.
Derive conclusions from a knowledge base using resolution.
Show patience and rigor when verifying multi-step logical proofs.

weekly_schedule.description: Probability, conditional independence, and Bayes' rule.

lesson_outcomes.text: State Bayes' rule and explain its role in reasoning under uncertainty.
Compute posterior probabilities for diagnostic scenarios using Bayes' rule.
Acknowledge uncertainty honestly when reporting AI-based conclusions.

weekly_schedule.description: Structure, inference, and applications of Bayesian networks.

lesson_outcomes.text: Describe how a Bayesian network encodes conditional dependencies.
Construct a small Bayesian network and query it for probabilities.
Justify modeling assumptions with reference to available data.

weekly_schedule.description: Learning paradigms, training and testing data, and overfitting.

lesson_outcomes.text: Differentiate supervised, unsupervised, and reinforcement learning.
Split a dataset into training and test sets and evaluate a baseline model.
Demonstrate responsible handling of datasets, including proper attribution.

weekly_schedule.description: Decision trees, k-nearest neighbors, and evaluation metrics.

lesson_outcomes.text: Explain how decision trees and k-nearest neighbors classify new examples.
Train a classifier and compute accuracy, precision, and recall.
Defend model selection decisions using measured results.
Describe the structure of a feedforward neural network and the role of backpropagation.
Train a simple neural network on a small dataset using a library.
Practice systematic experimentation by recording and comparing training runs.

weekly_schedule.description: Text preprocessing, representation, and basic language tasks.

lesson_outcomes.text: Outline the main stages of a basic natural language processing pipeline.
Build a text classifier using tokenization and a bag-of-words representation.
Demonstrate sensitivity to linguistic and cultural diversity when selecting text data.

weekly_schedule.description: Fairness, transparency, accountability, privacy, and AI governance.

lesson_outcomes.text: Identify sources of bias, privacy risk, and accountability gaps in AI systems.
Evaluate a case study of an AI system against fairness and transparency criteria.
Advocate responsible AI practices in team discussions and project decisions.
Summarize the AI techniques applied in the final project.
Demonstrate a working AI solution to a defined problem.
Accept feedback professionally and reflect on areas for improvement.
